## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Raṭṭhapālattheragāthā* (Thag 16.4) is a verse composition attributed to the elder Raṭṭhapāla, preserved in the sixteenth nipāta of the *Theragāthā* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into several modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. In early post-canonical and paracanonical literature, verses or themes from the text are cited or referenced in the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), the *Paccekabuddhaapadāna* (Tha-Ap 2), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2), and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 9, Ne 37) [SuttaCentral].

The text shares extensive material across Buddhist and non-Buddhist Indian traditions. SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus both confirm that the core verses of Thag 16.4 (especially segments §7.4–20.4) directly correspond to the verses uttered in the *Raṭṭhapāla Sutta* of the Majjhima Nikāya (MN 82) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Verses are also shared within the Pali canon with the *Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā* (Thag 20.1), the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 147), the *Khaggavisāṇa Sutta* (Snp 1.3), and the Jātaka collection (*Kāmajātaka*, Ja 467; *Saṅkhapālajātaka*, Ja 524), as well as the Jain *Uttarādhyayanasūtra* (chapter 4) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus detects repeated stock verses shared with other Theragāthā poems (Thag 11.1, Thag 14.1) and multiple *Therī-apadāna* texts (Thi-Ap 19, 21, 22, 23, 24), alongside full commentary coverage in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].

Cross-language parallels and alignments are widely attested. Parallel verses occur in chapter 27 (*Paśyavarga* / Sight) of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* and its Tibetan translation, the Sanskrit *Patna Dharmapada*, and Chinese collections (T 210.19, T 212.28, T 213.27) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text with the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* parallel (T 26) and the individual translation *Lài zhā hé luó jīng* (賴吒和羅經, T 68), the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D 1), and passages in the *Lalitavistara* and *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna* [DharmaNexus].
